comments.text:
If you mean just standard DLSS/FSR upscaling, there won’t be a latency increase as the frame rate you see is the raw output from the GPU rendering at the internal resolution. 

There’s no frames being created by AI with those, just upscaling ,which means it will only be as fast as what your GPU already rendered the internal resolution at (barring a few percent less). From the other video, FSR4 performs better than DLSS (CNN) but trades blows with DLSS (Transformer). 

Main thing is that there is a bit of a performance penalty to FSR4 compared to DLSS (CNN) despite both being CNN based models. So there would be more “latency” in the way of there simply being less FPS. 

Any upscaling based solution, either DLSS or FSR4, will actually give you better latency for a simple fact of the GPU being able to render the lower internal resolution much faster. 

Think about it: if you have a 1080p internal resolution and a 1440p target to upscale to, you might get 15-20% more FPS rendering at 1080p instead of 1440p so even if you spent 5-10% on upscaling you’d still be getting a latency improvement as more frames are coming to the screen. 

Frame generation is a different story, and where discussions about latency truly matter, however. I don’t think it’s in any game thus far until launch where it’s supposedly going to be on Black Ops 6 so we will have to wait.

The transformer model in DLSS will be incredibly interesting, especially on older 20xx-40xx GPU’s as the performance hit is far larger than it is on the 50xx GPU’s. This will impact latency much further.
